archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A small, quick quarterback whose best plays come from leaving a muddy pocket and running for chunks. His passing is short, accurate and cautious, and it works only as well as his legs keep drives alive.

report.headline: Legs keep a below-average passing line afloat — if the hamstring allows
report.take:
Murray is quarterbacking a 5-1 team, but the record belongs mostly to the league's best defense: Minnesota ranks 1st in defensive EPA and 31st on offense. His passing line fits that picture. He is at -0.059 EPA per dropback, 31st of 49 and below the league's -0.002. He throws 170.3 yards a game and has a 3.2% touchdown rate, 34th. He is not a gunslinger here. His aggressiveness has dropped to 10.74% from 13% last year, and his average throw lands 1.6 yards short of the sticks. The completion work is sound: CPOE of 2.06 sits 2.8 points over the league average, and he is hitting 80.3% on throws of 0-9 air yards with a 9.8 CPOE.

The hidden drag is the screen game. His 33 throws behind the line have produced -0.508 EPA per play, which adds up to -16.8. That is a bigger hole than his whole dropback total of -8.3. Every other depth band is positive, and his 10-plus-yard throws run at +0.167. The scheme split tells the same story. Under center, which means play-action and moving launch points, he is at +0.189 a play. From shotgun he is at -0.214, and that is where 11 of his 15 sacks have come. Third down is the other leak: -0.302 EPA a play while facing 8.1 yards to go on average.

What holds it together is the running. His 16 scrambles have gained 157 yards and 8 first downs at +0.757 EPA each. His 4 designed runs have all been successes. He ranks 6th among quarterbacks in rushing yards a game. The sacks are the cost of that style, not a new flaw. An 8.9% sack rate (36th) and a 38.5% pressure-to-sack rate fit a career line that hit 0.5 last year and has never been good. Holding the ball 2.95 seconds to hunt for a lane produces both the sacks and the scrambles. Right now the scrambles are paying for them.

The real question is health. He left the opener after 17% of snaps, Carson Wentz started Week 2, and Wentz started again in Week 9 with Murray out with a hamstring strain. A hamstring is the worst injury for this profile. If it takes away his burst, he is left with the pocket game, and that has been below average. The last three games (+0.079 EPA per dropback, 17.4 PPR a game) show what a healthy Murray looks like in this offense: roughly league-average passing plus real rushing value.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for everything
strengths.body: His scrambles are the most efficient play in a bottom-two offense: +0.757 EPA each, with half of them moving the chains. He has been a top-tier rushing quarterback every year of his career, so this is who he is, not a hot streak. The only threat to it is the hamstring.

strengths.title: Accurate in the short game
strengths.body: Throws of 0-9 air yards are going for 80.3% completions and a 9.8 CPOE. His overall CPOE is 2.8 points over the league average. In the red zone he is at 14.9 CPOE with 4 touchdowns on 21 attempts. His career CPOE has swung year to year, but the short accuracy matches his better seasons.

strengths.title: Steady when the game is close late
strengths.body: In one-score fourth quarters he is at +0.145 EPA a play with a 75% completion rate and no interceptions. That matters on a team that plays almost every snap within one score behind an elite defense. It is a 43-play sample, so treat it as a lean, not a law.

concerns.title: Sacks are a career-long tax
concerns.body: An 8.9% sack rate ranks 36th, and 38.5% of his pressures end in sacks. Last year's pressure-to-sack rate was even worse, and it has been middling or poor every season. It comes from holding the ball to extend plays: his time to throw is up to 2.95. It will not go away. The question is only whether the scrambles keep outpaying it, and a bad hamstring would tip that balance.

concerns.title: Screens and shotgun are dead weight
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have cost -16.8 EPA, and shotgun snaps run at -0.214 a play against +0.189 under center. The screen number is extreme enough that some of it should regress. The shotgun gap, though, mirrors a third-down problem (-0.302 EPA a play) that reflects the offense's long-yardage struggles. Expect some of the screen damage to fade and the shotgun gap to persist.

concerns.title: Ball placement slipping
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate of 15.6% ranks 32nd of 42. That is close to last year's rate, which also ranked poorly, after three straight seasons near the top. When he opened up against Detroit with 27.6% aggressiveness, 28.6% of his throws were charted bad. Two straight years makes this look more like his current level than a blip.

trend.note: He climbed out of an ugly start: the Week 1 injury exit and a -12.1 EPA game at Tampa. Over the last three games he is at +0.079 EPA per dropback, though most of that lift comes from one sharp game in New Orleans; the others hovered near break-even. The hamstring now interrupts that path.

nextGame.headline: Hamstring first, Green Bay's top-five pass defense second
nextGame.body:
Green Bay's defense ranks 5th against the pass and 5th at limiting explosive passes, which is a poor fit for an offense that already struggles to move the ball through the air. The Packers sack quarterbacks at a 7% rate (11th), a real threat to a quarterback who takes sacks on 38.5% of his pressures. The openings are elsewhere. Green Bay's coverage of WR1s has been soft (2.3 PPR over their averages, 26th), and it sees an above-league share of targets going to receivers. That points the ball toward Justin Jefferson rather than T.J. Hockenson, who has been Murray's best target at 0.611 EPA a target. The Book has Minnesota as a 4.5-point underdog with a 41.5 total, which suggests a grinding, one-score game where his late-game steadiness and scrambles carry weight.

Availability drives everything. Murray was listed Out with a hamstring strain on November 9, and his estimated return date is the day of this game. That is an estimate, and Wentz started Week 9. If he plays at less than full speed, the scrambling that props up his line is the first thing to go. Jauan Jennings (calf) is also out, which costs snaps but little efficiency (-0.447 EPA a target), so more volume should funnel to Jefferson and Hockenson. On Green Bay's side, starting linebacker Zaire Franklin is out, which thins the middle-of-field coverage and the defenders who would chase him on scrambles. Micah Parsons has not played all season, so his absence is already built into the Packers' numbers. Green Bay's offense is also down a tackle, a guard and several backs against Minnesota's top-ranked defense, which supports the low-scoring script.

keyMatchups.title: Hockenson into the league's best TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay has held top tight ends furthest under their averages of any defense (-4.4 PPR, 1st). Hockenson has been Murray's most efficient outlet by a wide margin. Franklin's absence could loosen the middle, but the base expectation is a quieter day for the tight end and a heavier load on Jefferson.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush against his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: The Packers' 7% sack rate ranks 11th, and Murray's sack rate ranks 36th. Most of his sacks come from shotgun, so how often Kevin O'Connell keeps him under center will shape how many drives die. A hampered hamstring makes escaping pressure harder.

keyMatchups.title: Low-total, defense-first script
keyMatchups.body: A 41.5 total and a Minnesota defense ranked 1st point to a close, low-volume game, like most of his starts, which mostly went under. That caps his passing yards but rewards clean, mistake-free play and timely scrambles.

nextGame.watch: Whether he practices fully this week, and if he plays, whether he scrambles freely in the first half. If he is a pocket-only quarterback on Sunday, his floor drops sharply.

restOfSeason.body:
A healthy Murray in this offense is roughly a league-average passer with top-10 rushing value. That means modest passing totals in low-scoring games, a sack rate that stays high because it always has, and scrambles that keep him useful. Some of the season-long drag should ease. The screen damage is too extreme to persist at this level, and his touchdown rate (3.2%) sits below a red-zone line that has been efficient, so a small uptick in scoring is reasonable. The bad-throw rate and the shotgun and third-down struggles look structural, and with the defense carrying the team, the passing volume will not climb much.

The hamstring is the hinge. He has already missed two starts and left the opener early. A lingering strain would trim the rushing that separates him from a game manager. Expect rushing yards at the lower end of the range below until he shows his burst is back.
swingFactors: Hamstring recovery and whether he scrambles freely
How often the offense works under center versus shotgun
Jefferson and Hockenson staying healthy as Jennings sits

confidence.note: Active hamstring strain, two missed starts, and only about five full games of data.
